title: Indian Independence 1947
welcome_lead: From the Indian National Congress to the midnight of 14-15 August 1947, study the struggle that ended British rule.
meta_desc: History Independence Movements Adventure 1: Indian independence, Gandhi, Nehru, Jinnah and Partition.
final_note: You have travelled with Gandhi and Nehru to Tryst with Destiny. Partition's legacy still shapes South Asia.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gandhi's return from South Africa in 1915 transformed the Congress into a mass movement, with campaigns of non-cooperation (1920-22), the Salt March (1930) and the Quit India movement (August 1942). Subhas Chandra Bose's Indian National Army provided a different revolutionary strand.

Jinnah's articulation of the two-nation theory, the Lahore Resolution (1940) and the Cabinet Mission's failure produced the Mountbatten Plan. Lord Louis Mountbatten brought independence forward to 15 August 1947, partitioning British India into the dominions of India and Pakistan along the Radcliffe Line.

Nehru's 'Tryst with Destiny' speech welcomed independence at midnight 14-15 August 1947. Partition uprooted an estimated 10-15 million people and caused up to a million deaths. Gandhi was assassinated by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948. Disputes over Kashmir led to the first Indo-Pakistani War.
